raw_segments.text: Then he brought out and laid on the table all the things he had been keeping for fourteen
years that he thought would prove his crime—the jewels belonging to the murdered woman which
he had stolen to divert suspicion, a cross and a locket taken from her neck with a portrait
of her betrothed in the locket, her notebook and two letters—one from her betrothed,
telling her that he would soon be with her and her unfinished answer left on the table
to be sent off next day.
He carried off these two letters.
Why had he kept them for fourteen years afterwards, instead of destroying them as evidence against him?
